author: Patrick Commins Economics correspondent
description:
Andrew Hauser says central bank faces ‘hard choices’ as it looks to balance risks of entrenched inflation with desire to protect labour market

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Hauser, the Reserve Bank’s deputy governor, has reignited talk of a fifth interest rate hike on Melbourne Cup day, warning of “hard choices” ahead in response to an inflation outlook that “looks materially worse” than the central bank had expected two months ago.

Hauser, speaking at an investment bank conference in Sydney on Wednesday morning, said the RBA monetary policy board members were juggling a slowing economy with fears that Australians were starting to lose faith in the central bank’s ability to bring inflation back to the 2.5% t
title: Odds of fifth interest rate hike this year likely to shorten as RBA deputy warns inflation outlook ‘worsening’

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Toforest Johnson’s death penalty reduced to life in prison without parole over doubts about his conviction

Toforest Johnson, an Alabama death row inmate, will no longer face execution after the state’s Republican governor commuted his sentence amid increasing doubts about his conviction.

Kay Ivey, the Alabama governor, commuted Johnson’s sentence to life in prison without parole in the 1995 murder of William Hardy, a Jefferson county deputy sheriff. Johnson has long maintained he is innocent, and several former public officials, as well the local district attorney, have argued he should receive a new trial.

Continue reading...
title: Alabama governor commutes sentence of prisoner on death row

author: Robert Mackey
description:
Anti-Defamation League post decries ‘shylock’ slur but does not explain that president used it at Kansas rally on Monday

The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) denounced the use of the term “shylock” as antisemitic on Tuesday, without explaining that the slur had been used a day earlier by Donald Trump in a speech in Kansas.

Trump used the slur during a Monday night rally in support of Republican senator Roger Marshall, who is locked in a closer-than-expected re-election fight against Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton. Marshall, a doctor, as been criticized for filing lawsuits against more than 700 patients with outstanding bills, leading to 18 of them being arrested.

Continue reading...
title: ADL condemns Trump’s antisemitic slur but fails to mention him by name

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
After being contacted by officers, politician says, he has paid bill and is ‘grateful for the team at the servo for their understanding’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

On Tuesday night, Ben Carroll received a phone call: police were looking for him.

The Victorian premier had met with the state’s police commissioner earlier that morning – so he wasn’t exactly hard to find.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I forgot to pay’: Victoria’s premier Ben Carroll drives off without paying for petrol, sparking police inquiries

author: Donna Lu assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
Study identifies ‘circadian depression’ as affecting nearly a quarter of more than 11,000 participants

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian researchers have identified a new subtype of depression – termed “circadian depression” – linked to disruptions in the body’s internal clock, which they believe is less responsive to traditional antidepressant treatments.

In a study published in British Journal of Psychiatry, involving clinical and genetic data from 11,380 Australians with mostly severe and recurrent depression, researchers identified circadian depression as affecting nearly a quarter (23%) of participants.
title: Australian researchers identify new subtype of depression linked to body clock disruptions

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Kennedy taught in New York public schools and advocated for disability rights after suffering severe spinal cord injury

Kyle Kennedy, the granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy, has died at the age of 42.

Kyle, the daughter of Michael Kennedy, who died in 1997, and Victoria Gifford Kennedy, “passed away peacefully” on 21 September at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, according to her obituary published by Burke Funeral Homes.

Continue reading...
title: Kyle Kennedy, granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy, dies aged 42

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

  • Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured

  • Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament

The sister of murdered UK MP Jo Cox has said the attack on Australian MP Dr Helen Haines could be a moment for Australia to “find common ground” and change the way politics is practised in this country.

Cox was killed in 2016, shot and stabbed by a far-right extremist outside a library as she prepared to meet with constituents.
title: Helen Haines live updates: Sister of slain UK MP Jo Cox urges Australians to find ‘common ground’; alleged Haines attacker to face court

author: Ariana Baio
description:
President makes suggestion while announcing new program to reward tipsters who submit fraud allegations

Donald Trump suggested on Tuesday that he would serve as “the arbitrator” of decisions in the justice department’s new anti-fraud program that awards compensation to those who submit tips resulting in conviction or significant federal enforcement.

While announcing the new program alongside JD Vance, the vice-president, who leads the White House’s taskforce to eliminate fraud, the president told reporters he had a solution for situations where multiple people submit a tip for the same alleged fraud.
title: Trump suggests he could be ‘arbitrator’ in DoJ anti-fraud whistleblower scheme

author: Sam Levine
description:
The statement revealed in court papers raises questions about the reliability of the list of 20,000 people in California

The justice department’s list of suspected non-citizens in California includes a “high percentage” of people born in the United States, Los Angeles election officials said on Tuesday.

The statement, made in court papers, raises further questions about the reliability of a list of 20,000 people the justice department provided to election officials in Los Angeles last week. The department sent the county and California secretary of state the list last week and gave them a 48-hour deadline to segregate ballots cast from anyone on the list unless they could verify their citizenship. California election officials refused and the Department of Justice
title: DoJ’s suspected non-citizens list includes ‘high percentage’ of those born in US, LA officials say

author: Luke Harding
description:
Advance warnings of missile attacks were seemingly suspended last week by the White House, but Ukraine’s president says: ‘Now it works’

The US has resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv about Russian missile strikes, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday after a meeting with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine was again receiving advance warnings of ballistic missile attacks, which were seemingly suspended last week by the White House. “Now it works. It’s great,” he said, saying the US move would save lives.

Continue reading...
title: US has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine about Russian strikes, says Zelenskyy

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns

Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook.

The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau

author: Chris Stein
description:
Amy Acton’s brother calls campaigning on his sister’s sexual abuse from their mother’s husband ‘a despicable low’

The family of Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio, is criticizing her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy for using Acton’s estranged mother in a recently released campaign ad.

In the ad, which has circulated among conservatives on social media, her mother, Donna Arthur, said: “She says she grew up living in a tent. None of that is true. She’s lied her entire life.”

Continue reading...
title: Ohio Democrat’s family criticizes Vivek Ramaswamy for bringing up estranged mother in gubernatorial ad

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Move signals Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea industry but threatens to undermine Labour’s green credentials

The Jackdaw gasfield will be given the go-ahead on Wednesday, in a move that signals Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea industry but threatens to trigger a row with climate campaigners and Labour MPs.

Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, and John Healey, the chancellor, will make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning after more than a year of deliberations over whether doing so would violate the UK’s climate commitments.

Continue reading...
title: Jackdaw North Sea gasfield to get go-ahead in blow to climate campaigners

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home after gig was one of most painful experiences of her life

A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard.

She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”

Continue reading...
title: Russell Brand told woman to ‘clear up the mess you’ve made’ after alleged rape, court hears

author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
description:
Mounting anxiety as Russia’s war on Ukraine reaches Nato’s borders with targeting of vessels transporting agricultural cargo

Nato is deploying additional military assets to the Black Sea amid the recent deadly escalation of Russian attacks on merchant shipping, as five more vessels were attacked on Tuesday.

Russia’s military said it ⁠struck ​three cargo vessels in Ukraine’s ⁠port of Reni and two ⁠other cargo vessels en ​route ‌to ‌Odesa.

Continue reading...
title: Nato increases Black Sea deployment amid escalating deadly Russian attacks

author: Hannah Al-Othman, North of England Correspondent
description:
Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after doctors put her symptoms down to Covid-19

A baby girl who died from meningitis may have been saved if doctors had tested her for the infection sooner, rather than putting her symptoms down to Covid, an inquest jury has found.

Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023, days after she was taken into the emergency department with a high temperature and vomiting.

Continue reading...
title: Baby who died from meningitis may have been saved if tested sooner, inquest finds

author: Ariana Baio in New York
description:
GOP lawmakers threaten to pull support for president’s agenda after Russia diesel deal and sanctions pause

  • US politics live – latest updates

A handful of Republicans have spoken out against Donald Trump’s softening stance on Russia, threatening to pull financial support for his agenda over his “embarrassing” handling of the Ukraine war.

Don Bacon, an outgoing congressman in Nebraska, condemned Trump’s actions – which include a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel and the
title: Republicans push back on Donald Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine

author: Anna Betts
description:
The ex-student writes she wants to share information that ‘may be relevant’ to vote of no confidence

The former Cornell University student who accused seven men of sexually assaulting her at a fraternity house in 2024 recently wrote a letter to campus faculty leaders saying that she felt “unsupported and disbelieved” by the Ivy League institution’s president.

The letter addressed to the Cornell faculty senate was obtained and published by the New York Times on Tuesday – and in it the former student said she wanted to share information that she believed “may be relevant” as the panel considers a vote of no confid
title: Ex-student alleging sexual assault felt ‘unsupported’ by Cornell president

author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
description:
Latest report paints a painful picture of the care sector during the pandemic. But timid recommendations and a lack of accountability threaten to undermine it

Of all 10 reports due to be published by the long-running Covid-19 inquiry, this week’s findings on adult social care were especially anticipated.

The impact of Covid-19 on the care sector was calamitous: tens of thousands of people died, staff were forced to wear bin bags due to a lack of protective clothing and relatives were banned from seeing their loved ones in their dying days.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Superficial damp squib’: Covid inquiry recommendations fail to impress bereaved families

author: Aisha Down
description:
Outage shows danger of growing reliance on small number of big companies for our digital infrastructure, say experts

It happened again. A power outage hit a datacentre in London, and things cascaded from there: multiple banking services faltered, court hearings were put on hold and patients reported temporary glitches on the NHS app.

The datacentre in question was in Google’s europe-west2-b zone, one of over a dozen “zones” that the US search giant maintains in Europe to service its clients.

Continue reading...
title: Power outage at Google datacentre in London causes widespread disruption

author: Jon Henley in Paris
description:
French state places officers as agents of authority tasked with repressing, rather than managing, public dissent

Familiar images of teargas clouds drifting across Paris squares, police baton charges against masked protesters and terrified teenagers floored – and worse – by stun grenades have once again focused the world’s attention on France’s policing methods.

While most of its western European neighbours generally favour police tactics that prioritise crowd containment and de-escalation, France has long responded to social movements that take to the streets with, at times, shocking physical force.

Continue reading...
title: France’s culture of violent policing means the battle for its streets is far from over

author: Maya Yang
description:
Videos show shark launching several feet from water as a group of friends pose for photos along Marina state beach

A great white shark put on a spectacular display for California beachgoers over the weekend, leaping from the water off Marina state beach and photobombing visitors.

Videos circulating online show a great white shark launching several feet out of the water in the background as a group of friends pose for photos along the beach.

Continue reading...
title: Great white shark leaps from water and photobombs California beachgoers

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Union furious as bank scraps remote-first policy from February 2027, requiring its nearly 40,000 UK employees to come in at least twice a week

NatWest has ordered 13,000 staff to increase their in-office days from two days per month to two days per week, angering its staff union.

The banking group, which serves customers under the Royal Bank of Scotland, NatWest, and Coutts brands, will require all of its nearly 40,000 UK staff to follow a strict two days per week office schedule from February 2027, abolishing a remote-first policy for thousands of employees.

Continue reading...
title: NatWest cracks down on 13,000 staff attending office two days a month

author: Associated Press
description:
Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird

A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel.

Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel

author: Dara Kerr
description:
Coyote euthanized after reportedly roaming Atwater Village comfortably for months and attacking one-year-old boy

One Los Angeles neighborhood has been at war over a wild coyote, and over the weekend it all came to a head.

For months, the animal had been roaming the trendy Atwater Village, showing up in broad daylight, sleeping in back yards and approaching residents. At least one person had reportedly fed the coyote and others affectionately nicknamed it Wiley. But some residents feared the creature had become dangerously too cozy.

Continue reading...
title: Trendy LA neighborhood’s war over wild coyote erupts after child attacked

author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
description:
Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody it

To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.

But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.

Continue reading...
title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Lawyers tell inquiry ‘patients’ lives are at stake’ through improper use of Oxevision system for most vulnerable

Families bereaved by the misuse of an “intrusive” camera monitoring system for vulnerable patients used in half of England’s mental health wards, have called for it to be banned to help prevent more avoidable deaths.

Lawyers for the families said “patients’ lives are at stake” by the continuing use of Oxevision, the Lampard inquiry into mental health deaths in Essex heard on Tuesday.

The inquiry was told that five patients killed themselves, or died unexpectedly, in two years while being surveilled by Oxevision’s infrared cameras at Essex Partnership University NHS foundation trust (Eput).

Peter Mant KC, representing more than 70 bereaved families, including the family of Elise Sebastian, 16, who killed herself in 2021 when staff had muted Oxevision’s alarm system, said: “Use of this technology has contributed in material ways
title: Ban ‘intrusive’ cameras on mental health wards in England, say bereaved families

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Conflict in Middle East is pushing jet fuel costs higher and many carriers are not hedged against such increases, Michael O’Leary says

Ryanair’s chief executive has predicted a record increase in European air fares next year, as airlines grapple with fuel bills pushed higher by the Middle East conflict.

Many carriers are not hedged against rising jet fuel costs, Michael O’Leary said, which he predicted would lead to airline bankruptcies and takeovers. He forecast these pressures would result in the price of plane tickets rising by as much as 20%.

Continue reading...
title: European air fares could rise by as much as 20% in 2027, Ryanair boss predicts

author: Ben Quinn
description:
Andrew Young claims he received ‘menacing’ call from man who introduced himself as Robinson

The far-right activist known as Tommy Robinson threatened to publish details about a journalist’s family and warned him that they would have to move home, a court has been told.

The alleged threats were said to have been made in a telephone call by Robinson to one of a number of journalists involved in reporting on his activities after the 2024 Southport killings, when he was accused of influencing the subsequent riots.

Continue reading...
title: Tommy Robinson threatened to publish details about journalist’s family, court told

author: Rob Davies
description:
Flutter says one in 10 UK and Ireland workers at risk of redundancy because of a ‘material increase in betting and gaming duties’

  • Business live – latest updates

The gambling company behind Paddy Power and SkyBet has announced up to 1,400 job cuts, blaming tax rises imposed by Rachel Reeves.

Flutter Entertainment revealed plans on Tuesday to restructure its UK and Ireland division, affecting staff in Leeds, Dublin and Sunderland. Redundancies are also expected to hit offices in Porto in Portugal and Cluj-Napoca in Romania.

Continue reading...
title: Paddy Power owner blames tax rises for plan to shed up to 1,400 jobs

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
The Married … with Children actor says the news is ‘unnerving’ and ‘really confusing’

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

After becoming a prominent advocate for multiple sclerosis awareness and chronicling her struggles in an emotional memoir published in March, the Emmy-winning actor Christina Applegate has revealed she does not have the debilitating autoimmune disease after all.

Applegate, 54, made the stunning announcement in an episode of her podcast MeSsy, recorded with fel
title: Actor Christina Applegate reveals she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
‘Deeply troubling’ messages came to light during investigation into misuse of Flock camera system

Five officers resigned recently from a North Carolina police agency – and a sixth remained suspended – after they allegedly exchanged racist texts.

The chief of the Charlotte-Mecklenburg police department (CMPD) said the messages came to light during an investigation into misuse of its Flock camera system.

Continue reading...
title: Discovery of North Carolina police officers’ alleged racist texts prompts review of arrest records

author: Press Association
description:
Corporation announces broadcast closures and job losses in effort to find savings of £500m

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The BBC will close BBC Three, BBC Scotland and BBC Radio 4 Extra linear broadcast services in spring 2027 as part of cost-cutting measures.

In addition, about 100 jobs will be cut at BBC News, as the corporation faces pressure to make savings of £500m by 2028.

Continue reading...
title: BBC Three and BBC Scotland TV channels to be shut down next year

author: Jason Wilson
description:
Timmy Teepell’s firm paid $250,000 by America Next, which has been trying to gin up ‘organic’ opposition to El-Sayed

  • Man who heckled El-Sayed is former Josh Hawley aide, records show

The man who attempted to ambush the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed with a question about his supposed allegiance to the Muslim Brotherhood – which El-Sayed parlayed into a viral clip for his campaign – is the son of a political operator who recently received $250,000 for “canvassing and influencer marketing” against El-Sayed, the Guardian has learned.

In the now-famous exchange, a man – first identified by the Handbasket as Thomas “Tommy” Teepell – asked El-Sayed if he would “disavow” the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said he would, but then asked: “What are yo
title: Michigan heckler the son of Republican adviser paid for ‘influencer marketing’ against El-Sayed

author: Shrai Popat
description:
President to stump for Michael Whatley, who is facing an uphill battle against Democrat Roy Cooper for the Senate, as elections are just two weeks away

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Welcome to the US politics live blog! I’m Shrai Popat and I’ll be bringing you the latest lines from Washington and beyond.

We start today with Donald Trump’s upcoming to trip to Greenville, North Carolina – where he’ll stump for Michael Whatley, the Republican nominee for US Senate, facing an uphill battle against Roy Cooper, the state’s former Democratic governor who has consistently led Whatley in the polls for the open seat.
title: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in North Carolina – US politics live

author: Kari Paul in San Francisco
description:
Developers propose turning San Francisco Centre into not a server-based facility but a ‘community-based AI exhibit’

Downtown San Francisco has shown signs of revival since being battered by the Covid pandemic, which led to what many called a “doom loop” of vacant buildings, a worsening homelessness crisis, and dwindling public transit. But one highly visible reminder of the city’s struggle to recover remains: the San Francisco Centre mall, which sits at the heart of these urban renewal efforts and has been conspicuously boarded up since January of this year.

A number of ideas have been floated for the mall’s reopening, including a multi-level sports complex, <
title: Downtown datacenter? AI plan floated for boarded-up San Francisco mall

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Stricken UK water supplier lines up John Hutton as independent chair designate if takeover goes ahead

The group of Thames Water creditors pursuing a £10bn rescue deal for Britain’s largest water supplier has lined up a former senior Labour minister to chair the company, as it tries to win over the government.

The creditor consortium, called London & Valley Water, said on Tuesday that Lord John Hutton had been selected as independent chair designate of the Thames Water board, if the consortium’s takeover of the utility goes ahead.

Continue reading...
title: Thames Water creditors secure former Labour minister to drive rescue deal

author: Martin Belam
description:
The DoJ has charged 28 green card holders in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote. Plus, is the world really ready for AI actors?

Good morning. The US Department of Justice has charged 28 green card holders in California, accusing them of fraudulently registering to vote and casting illegal ballots. The arrests – 11 people are in custody – mark the latest escalation in federal efforts against alleged noncitizen voting.

The crackdown comes days after the DOJ sued California to block the state from tabulating certain ballots in November’s midterms. California’s secretary of state, Shirley Weber, called the demands “outrageous”, pointing out that federal officials have spent months making “vague and unsubstantiated allegations”. Democrats and voting rights groups say the administration is laying the groundwork to sow doubt over November’s election re
title: Federal efforts over alleged noncitizen voting escalate with California arrests | First Thing

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Conservative leader to give a speech later, while Treasury sources say Healey has ruled out a rise in capital gains tax

Criminals including killers and sex offenders detained in hospital will no longer receive benefits under proposals called for by victims’ families, the Press Association reports. PA says:

The government confirmed the move to end so-called “double provision” which enables offenders to claim hundreds of pounds a month for living costs while receiving NHS psychiatric treatment.

Regulations laid in parliament today seek to close the loophole and prevent serious criminals receiving up to £800 a month in universal credit over several years, saving an estimated tens of millions of pounds annually.

We said we’d act to tackle this gross unfairness and we’re delivering on that promise.

For too long these violent criminals have had their living costs paid by the taxpayer twice over, while their victims and families paid the price.

Britain’
title: Badenoch says Healey’s budget will be worse than Reeves’s if he doesn’t slash spending – UK politics live

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Sébastien Lecornu suggests more curfews could be introduced to quell unrest after weekend protests

Meanwhile, president Emmanuel Macron has secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain during a tour of the Gulf, the French presidency said.

With the addition of deliveries from Saudi Arabia, France has commitments for 295,000 tonnes per month, representing just over 10 percent of its consumption, the presidency added.

Continue reading...
title: French cities ‘calm overnight’ after targeted curfews, prime minister says – Europe live

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Cabinet colleagues have previously called for an increase but chancellor feels it might ultimately cost the Treasury

John Healey will not raise capital gains tax in next week’s budget, despite previous calls to do so from cabinet colleagues including Louise Haigh and Wes Streeting.

The chancellor has decided that any increase might ultimately cost the Treasury if wealthy individuals defer the sale of assets or move them out of the country, according to Treasury sources.

Continue reading...
title: Healey to reject calls to raise capital gains tax in budget

author: Phillip Inman Senior economics writer
description:
ONS data shows rate down from 4.9% but number of job vacancies continues to shrink

  • Business live – news updates

Unemployment in the UK fell unexpectedly in the three months to August, to 4.7% from 4.9%.

The Office for National Statistics figures, which provide a backdrop to the budget on 28 October, also showed that the number of payrolled employees rose by 13,000 between August and September, to 30.3m.

Continue reading...
title: Surprise drop in UK unemployment to 4.7%

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
Online betting was the ‘direct and paramount’ cause behind Kyle Hudson’s decision to take his own life, inquest finds

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Kyle Hudson was “a young man brimming with promise”, with a loving and supportive partner, family and friends, and prospects.

“It was a near ideal picture – except for the grip that online sports betting had upon him,” the Victorian coroner Paul Lawrie said on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: A young life ‘dominated by gambling’: Victorian coroner delivers stinging findings on death of 22-year-old

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Coroner says she’s considering adopting recommendations from Victoria’s cults inquiry as investigation into Elizabeth Struh’s death continues

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The coroner investigating the death of Elizabeth Struhs is considering adopting recommendations from Victoria’s cults inquiry, warning a “lack of curiosity” about her family’s religious beliefs was a “missed opportunity”.

Elizabeth, an eight-year-old, died on 7 January 2022 of diabetic ketoacidosis after her father ceased providing insulin to treat type 1 diabetes.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Lack of curiosity’ about family’s religious beliefs was ‘missed opportunity’ to save eight-year-old, inquest hears

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: The prime minister’s campaign against noisy passengers has struck a chord with commuters. Whether anyone hears him remains to be seen.

Good morning.

Me again, back from the October school holiday (a week in glorious Wales, thanks for asking) and ready to hear your commuter woes. For our prime minister, it’s “one of the most annoying things on public transport”: maybe you’re trying to work, or read, or you’ve finally got your kid to sleep, when someone starts blasting sound from their phone at full volume.

France | The prime minister has said he has asked regional authorities to impose partial curfews in some cities after the government admitted police had “lost control” in several places during violent weekend protests around the country.

UK politics | Andy Bu
title: Tuesday briefing: Can Andy Burnham beat Britain’s headphone dodgers?

author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
description:
Critics said images of detained former leader were a stunt by the military to end country’s diplomatic isolation

Myanmar has delivered presents from Britain’s ​King Charles to Aung San Suu Kyi, releasing rare photos of the imprisoned former leader in what critics said was a stunt by the country’s military to end diplomatic isolation.

A presidential spokesperson said on social media that home ministry officials handed over two gardening books on soil, “along with one sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch”, from King Charles, who is known to have an interest in planting and the environment.

Continue reading...
title: Myanmar’s ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi seen in rare photos after receiving gift from King Charles

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Selina Cartmell announces season including Stockport-set version of Phaedra myth by Simon Stephens

A theatre boss has promised to channel the “pioneering spirit of Manchester” and be “brave and fearless” as she unveiled a new season of work, two years after a deeply damaging censorship row.

Selina Cartmell, the artistic director of the Royal Exchange in Manchester, revealed details of 2027-28 productions that include a retelling of the Munich air disaster and a modern Stockport-set version of the ancient Greek myth Phaedra.

Continue reading...
title: Royal Exchange boss unveils new plays two years after damaging censorship row

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Transport hub will offer through trains between Leeds and Manchester with ‘turn-up-and-go’ service

A new railway station will be built in Bradford to “transform how people travel across the north”, the government has announced.

The station will be at the heart of the Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR) scheme, built on the current Bradford Interchange site but allowing through trains between Leeds and Manchester.

Continue reading...
title: New Bradford railway station will ‘transform travel across the north’

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Rise in economic hardship and changes in attitudes towards migration could explain drop in support, experts say

Public support for the NHS’s founding principles – that it is free to use, available to everyone and tax-funded – has fallen over the last five years, research has shown.

Backing for all three pillars dropped between 2021 and 2025 across the UK population, except for a small rise in millennials’ support for the NHS being funded from taxation.

Continue reading...
title: Public support for founding principles of NHS is falling across UK population

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Witness breaks down in tears, tells court ‘I was scared’ after son declined to report alleged kissing and touching by broadcaster

  • Listen to the podcast Alan Jones on Trial

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

The mother of the youngest alleged victim of Alan Jones has told a Sydney court she “trusted” the 2GB broadcaster and was “comfortable” her teenager was going to spend a weekend at his Fitzroy Falls property.

The young man, known as complainant A, has testified that when he was 17 he was alone at the southern highlands farm when Jones allegedly ki
title: Mother of alleged Alan Jones victim ‘absolutely trusted’ the radio host, court told

author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Eleanor Biggs and Rudi Zygadlo
description:
The bestselling author says her books will no longer be supplied to UK bookshops over fears of prosecution. Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique report

For now there might be a copy or two of Intermezzo left kicking around in your local bookshop – snap it up if you haven’t already, because soon that will be it.

Last year, Sally Rooney said she would be using her royalties to support Palestine Action, a group that is proscribed as a terrorist organisation under UK law. Since then, thousands of people have been arrested for supporting the group. Now, faced with the risk of prosecution under terrorism legislation, Rooney and her publishers have decided to stop supplying her books to retailers in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Why terrorism laws stopped Sally Rooney selling books in the UK – podcast

author: Douglas Smith Indigenous affairs reporter
description:
Northern Territory government announced sweeping reforms of child protection sector in May, just days after the Warlpiri girl was found dead

• Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A report into the Northern Territory’s child protection sector has detailed “confronting” and “heartbreaking” failures in the lead-up to the alleged murder of Warlpiri girl Kumanjayi Little Baby.

The five-year-old was found dead in April, five days after she was allegedly abducted from a town camp in Alice Springs.
title: Kumanjayi Little Baby: damning report finds ‘heartbreaking’ child protection failures before five-year-old’s death

author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
description:
Bank says bulk of redundancies will occur before end of year, citing challenging economy, competition and ‘rapid technological change’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

National Australia Bank is cutting 2,500 jobs, representing 6% of its workforce, marking another significant round of cuts in a sector heavily exposed to disruption by artificial intelligence.

NAB said in a statement on Tuesday that the bulk of the redundancies would occur before the end of the year, citing a challenging economy, competition and “rapid technological change”.

title: NAB to cut 2,500 jobs in massive restructure
